## Purpose

Request a completed epic's ordinary aggregate verification without reopening its
children or editing legacy checkpoint state. A released branch owner is allowed.

## When a playbook uses it

A project supervisor can use this after a completed container has collected its
children but still lacks current aggregate evidence. Preview first, then apply
with the returned `head_sha` and an attributable reason.

## How it works internally

`IntegrationCommandsMixin` checks integration operator authority and calls
`TrainControls.reverify_epic` in `src/integration/train_controls.py`. Apply repeats
the source identity and writer checks, wakes normal target backoff, and requests
one serialized, bounded train visit. The ordinary recursive readiness evaluator
still requires current child containment, exact checks and accepted tree reviews.

## Side effects and persistence

Preview writes no domain state. Apply records
`integration.epic_reverification_requested` and
`integration.epic_reverification_observed` events with the principal, reason,
head and completion identities. The train may advance its ordinary batch or
completion protocol. Only that protocol writes passing Git provenance and
`task_completion_records`; the control never manufactures a verification pass.

## Failure modes and diagnostics

`changed` means the previewed head or observed refs moved; preview again.
`refused` names an eligibility, ownership, writer or Git observation problem.
`pending` means train admission deferred the visit, including repository
concurrency or provider rate limits. `visited` reports the actual `state`,
`blockers` and completion identity and does not itself mean PASS. Inspect
`aq integration status PROJECT` for the target's continuing progress.

## Example

```bash
aq integration reverify-epic prime-forge-80
aq integration reverify-epic prime-forge-80 --apply \
  --head <head_sha-from-preview> --reason "Verify the collected aggregate"
```
